analysis:
Examined ProviderLoop+Serve.swift (head 429-430) and ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery.swift (patch 15-48). Serve.swift change: on the control-reader task, an `.inferenceRequest` event now calls noteCoordinatorRequest() and then falls through to the work FIFO as before. That handler only stamps coordinatorConnection.lastRequestAt when connected; it does not touch admission, decryption, or the grant (clearConnectionAuthorization, handleTrustStatus). Request admission is unchanged and still depends on the existing App Attest/legacy gating (T-052, T-053). The change is local-state bookkeeping.

Recovery file change: superviseServingAuthorization now delegates to ServingReadiness.verdict(connection:trust:now:), which is not supplied. The previous logic reset the reconnect attempts counter on current App Attest authorization or path=="legacy". The new logic resets it on .authorized and treats .pending/.unconfirmed/nil as non-evidence. It clears unauthorizedSince instead of reconnecting. A coordinator-routed request is treated as newer than an earlier refusal (lastRequestAt). A remaining question is whether ServingReadiness could let a stale or revoked grant look authorized from a request alone. This is status/doctor display and re-register supervision logic only. It does not appear to feed request-time authorization, which is enforced by the coordinator per T-053 (platform-owned). Also unverified: whether .authorized still requires the hasCurrentAppAttestAuthorization expiry check, and whether a coordinator that stops repeating refusals could suppress recovery re-registration (availability, T-057). Neither is established by the supplied evidence, so no finding. A deeper look at ServingReadiness and DaemonState.CoordinatorConnection.lastRequestAt persistence is useful but not blocking.

No new attack surface, key handling, or data exposure is introduced. T-041, TB-012 and other cache or add-on threats are untouched.
